contests.title: El Dorado — Data centers and battery storage ordinance

provenance.quote: Shall the following be adopted: “An Ordinance of the City of El Dorado, Kansas, prohibiting the installation and operation of High Impact Data Centers (defined as data centers with a peak electrical load exceeding ten (10) megawatts, or a daily water draw exceeding one hundred thousand (100,000) gallons) and Tier 2 and Tier 3 battery energy storage systems (defined as systems with an aggregate energy capacity greater than 80kWh). If adopted, this Ordinance shall remain in effect for ten (10) years and may not be repealed or amended during that period except by a vote of the electors.”

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Prohibits covered large data centers and Tier 2 or Tier 3 battery-storage systems throughout El Dorado. The proposed ordinance defines which facilities are covered, excludes ordinary accessory computer equipment and vehicle batteries, and prevents smaller battery systems from being combined to evade the ban. During the first ten years, any repeal or amendment would require another vote of the people.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the ordinance prohibiting the covered data centers and battery-storage systems.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not adopt this proposed ordinance.

parts.label: Data centers
parts.what: Covers facilities mainly used for bulk data processing, storage or transmission that need more than 10 megawatts of peak electricity or draw more than 100,000 gallons of water per day. Ordinary office servers, school computer labs and manufacturing controls that are secondary to a building’s main use are excluded.

parts.label: Battery systems and a difference in the official texts
parts.what: The ballot summary describes battery systems above 80 kilowatt-hours. The full ordinance also places a room or enclosed area with more than one storage technology in Tier 2, even without stating a minimum capacity for that alternative. Tier 2 and Tier 3 systems would be prohibited. Stand-alone 12-volt car batteries and electric vehicles are excluded.

parts.label: Smaller systems used together
parts.what: Single-technology Tier 1 systems of 80 kilowatt-hours or less can remain subject to applicable codes. Several smaller systems cannot be arranged to function as a prohibited larger system. The City would consider total capacity, shared equipment or controls, integrated operation and proximity on the same or commonly controlled adjacent parcels.

parts.label: Where the ban applies
parts.what: Applies in every zoning district and to every land-use category within the city. Violations would face the civil and criminal penalties in the City’s existing zoning regulations; this measure does not specify a new dollar fine.

parts.label: Ten-year voter protection
parts.what: The ballot language requires voter approval for amendment or repeal during the first ten years. The state law cited in the proposed ordinance lets the governing body amend or repeal a petition ordinance after ten years. The published ordinance gives no automatic expiration date.
